pl-l2d29c4-d1e108.summary: Explains that since by sin man already had a body subject to death, God, speaking as if angry about proud man, says to the angels: beware lest he eat of the tree of life, of which he is unworthy; had he persisted he would have eaten and lived forever. As he said in word, he did in deed, sending him from the paradise of delight to a fitting place, as an evil man among the good who will not change is expelled from their company.
claims: Man's unworthiness, not the tree's power, is the point.

pl-l2d29c4.summary: Interprets Genesis 3:22: since by sin man already had a body subject to death, the words are God's speaking as if angry: 'beware, angels, lest he eat from the tree of life, of which he is unworthy'; had he persisted he would have eaten and lived forever, but by disobedience he is unworthy. What God said in word he showed in deed, sending man out to a place suited to him, as an evil man living among the good who will not change is expelled from their company.
claims: By sin man's body was already subject to death.
Genesis 3:22 expresses God's anger and man's unworthiness.
Had man persisted, he would have eaten from the tree of life and lived forever.
Man was expelled to a place suited to his condition.
